summary: A message sent while the agent works can steer the running turn (read at the agent's next step) or be queued until the turn ends. Measured against the Claude SDK: a mid-turn message with no priority is read at the next tool boundary, so Claude already steered; priority 'later' waits for the turn to finish. Codex steers through turn/steer; OpenCode cannot take a mid-turn message. Queueing is done by the backend: the client sends at once with delivery 'queue' on the turn envelope, Claude pushes it with priority 'later', and the Codex and OpenCode adapters hold it and start it when the running turn completes. The message therefore survives pane switches and closes, carries its pills and images through the ordinary send path, and each queued message is its own submission. Enter steers (Claude, Codex); Alt+Enter or the Queue button queues; OpenCode always queues. The backend advertises turn_queue_v1; a phone talking to an older backend keeps holding the message itself.

nativeAndroid.followUpRelease: Native Android composer gains the queue toggle; until then a mid-turn send steers on Claude and Codex, as it did before
